turns.text: it's 2:21 and i'm dead. need a plan to sleep thru the heat wave, no AC in my apt. just the steps pls, bullets only

Quick plan, assuming you're sleeping in the daytime:

- Close blinds/curtains on sun-facing windows before the day heats up
- Run any fans so they push hot air out, not just stir it around
- Cool the room before bed: damp towel or cold water on wrists/neck
- Light cotton sheets, no heavy blanket
- Cold water at bedside
- Avoid a hot shower right before bed; lukewarm is better

Tell me your setup (cooling, sleep hours) and I'll tighten it.
ok i just borrowed a portable unit from my mom, picked it up near her nail salon, have it til sunday. i sleep 8:30 to 3 after shift w blackout curtains and a box fan

Good, that helps:

- Put the portable unit in the bedroom and close the door; point it at the bed
- Start it 30-45 min before 8:30 so the room is already cool
- Vent its hose out a window and seal the gap with a towel or cardboard, otherwise it pulls hot air back in
- Box fan: turn it off while the unit runs. It stirs warm air and adds a bit of heat from the motor. Or aim it just to circulate cool air toward you
- Keep the blackout curtains shut; they help block heat
- Lukewarm shower, cold water at bedside
- Set the unit to its lowest comfortable temp, not max, so it doesn't run constantly

Want a version for before the shift too?
also does my thermos of cà phê sữa đá before shift mess w sleep in the heat

- Caffeine lasts hours, but you're drinking it for the shift, not before bed, so it's fine if the last of it is early in the night
- Stop caffeine about 6-8 hours before 8:30 a.m. sleep, so roughly by 1-2 a.m.
- Heat plus caffeine can make you feel more wired; sip water alongside
- Sweetened condensed milk is fine, just don't add a second thermos late
- If you need more, switch to ice water or decaf near the end of shift
